Algiers is a unique and underexplored tourist destination, offering a captivating blend of Mediterranean charm, rich history, and diverse architecture. Known for its whitewashed buildings cascading down towards the sea, the city is a mix of French colonial architecture, ancient Ottoman influences, and traditional Algerian culture. Visitors can explore the historic Casbah, a UNESCO World Heritage site, or stroll along the beautiful coastal promenades. Algiers’ less commercialized tourism scene allows for authentic experiences, from its bustling markets to its hidden neighbourhoods, making it an ideal destination for adventurous travelers seeking something off the beaten path. #algeria #algerie #pourtoii #fyypp #paratii

I take women’s rights seriously, so this is one of the first things I asked about while visiting Ghardaïa, Algeria  Now this is not necessarily for any reason. It has nothing to do with religion or location. The only thing it has to do with is that many communities that are small and follow old traditions typically give less rights and protections to women. However, I was pleasantly surprised that this is not the case in Ghardaia.   I really appreciate what I learned about  Mozabite communities, giving women in their own committees and ability to make decisions for themselves. When it comes to dress, extra protections, to feel safe and comfortable in their marriages, and the community standing in solidarity with its women. Places in Algeria that don’t feel real. 🇩🇿 The endless red dunes and towering rock formations of Tadrart. The remarkably preserved Roman ruins of Djemila, surrounded by mountains. The lush green forests of Seraïdi, overlooking the Mediterranean. And Constantine, a city built dramatically across cliffs and deep gorges, connected by bridges suspended high above the landscape. If Tadrart is on your list, you can experience it with  @duneyatours, our Tuareg-owned and operated agency based in Djanet. Travel deep into the Sahara by 4×4, camp beneath the stars, discover ancient rock art and experience the desert alongside the people who have travelled these lands for generations.
